confirmed: All three outcomes are scored on the PIT answers by raters, not self-reported. 'Two experts, blind to the experimental condition, independently evaluated three dimensions of the answers' on scales from 1 (worst) to 5 (best), with the rubric and example answers in Appendix 1. measure expert_raters fits (p. 13, Measures, Creative problem-solving; p. 40, Appendix 1).

The form does not overstate who rated the PIT. Only the UUT paragraph names the experts (first and last author) and says their two ratings were averaged. The PIT paragraph says only 'Two experts' and gives no rule for combining the two ratings (p. 12, Baseline originality; p. 13, Creative problem-solving).

AI was available while the scored output was produced. The experimental arm had ChatGPT-3.5 (Plus) open in a second browser tab during the PIT, and the control arm had no other open tab. The Figure 1 note repeats this. So ai_available 'yes', timing 'immediate' and question with_ai for three non-diversity constructs follow the codebook rule (p. 10, Experimental Procedure; p. 17, Figure 1 note; codebook section 1).

No after_ai outcome is missing. Participants solved two tasks: the UUT first, without ChatGPT in both arms, and then the PIT. Only self-report items came after the PIT (p. 10, Experimental Procedure; pp. 13-14, Measures).

Constructs match codebook section 6. Quality is 'the extent to which the answers match the goals provided', and Appendix 1 heads it 'usefulness for goals' (usefulness). Elaboration 'is measured by the amount of detail' (elaboration). Originality 'represents the uniqueness of the ideas' and runs from 'most common ideas' to 'unique ideas that are surprising', rated per answer (novelty). No rating compares different people's answers (so no diversity) or counts categories within one person (so no flexibility) (p. 13; p. 40, Appendix 1).

Unit participant is the unit of the paper's own analysis. The Table 2 t-tests have df 143 and the ANCOVAs F(1,142), which fit one score per participant for 68 + 77 = 145 students with no exclusions. The Figure 1 interaction also treats participants as units: 'individual participants created more original solutions with ChatGPT than they did without it' (p. 16, Table 2 and H1 text; p. 11, Table 1; p. 10; p. 17).

Every number in the three 'reported' strings matches the page images as printed. Table 2 rows 4-6: 2.99 (0.86) vs 3.60 (0.89), t 4.16, d 0.69; 2.21 (0.74) vs 2.79 (1.11), t 3.65, d 0.61; 2.21 (0.91) vs 2.74 (1.02), t 3.32, d 0.55; all p < .001. ANCOVAs F(1,142) = 19.07, 14.87 (printed 'p = <.001') and 12.56, partial eta squared .12, .10 and .08. Figure 1 tests: pre-test F(1,142) = 0.01, p = .928, partial eta squared .00; interaction F(1,142) = 7.79, p = .006, partial eta squared .05. Kappas .88, .93, .85 and arm Ns 68 and 77 also match (p. 16, Table 2 and H1 text; p. 17; p. 13; p. 11, Table 1).

The printed rows are internally consistent. Pooled-SD arithmetic at 68 and 77 gives d = 0.70, 0.61, 0.55 and t = 4.18, 3.65, 3.28, against printed 0.69, 0.61, 0.55 and 4.16, 3.65, 3.32. The gaps are within the rounding of two-decimal means (reviewer arithmetic; p. 16, Table 2).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The UUT is a pre-treatment baseline done without ChatGPT in both arms, so it answers none of them, and the form keeps its Table 2 row 1 numbers (1.74 vs 1.71, t = 0.18, p = .855, d = 0.03) in notes. The paper computes no diversity, fluency or flexibility measure. The bias indices subtract rescaled expert scores from self-evaluations, so they measure calibration, not creativity. Table 3 holds within-group correlations only (p. 10; p. 12; p. 14; p. 16, Table 2; p. 18, Table 3).

comparison_type ai_vs_bau and direction treatment_higher hold. The control arm had no other open tab, and although both arms could use the browser for other tools, 'no one chose to do so'. All three experimental means are higher, each with p < .001 (p. 10, Experimental Procedure; p. 16, Table 2).

primary 'not_stated' fits the text. H1a-c are three parallel sub-hypotheses, and the paper names no primary outcome. The introduction calls problem-solving performance 'the goal' but introduces five other components with 'More importantly'. Under codebook section 8, rule 2, originality (novelty rated by experts) would be the primary with_ai record either way. The preregistration itself was not checked (p. 4, Introduction; p. 8, H1; p. 9, preregistration statement).
summary: All three outcomes (PIT quality, elaboration and originality) are 1-5 ratings, by two experts blind to condition, of the answers that 145 randomized students wrote with or without ChatGPT open, so criterion 3 holds, and question with_ai, the constructs usefulness, elaboration and novelty, unit participant and AI availability all follow the codebook and the text. Every reported number matches Table 2 and the text on pages 16-17 as printed, and no outcome that bears on the three questions is missing, because the UUT is a pre-treatment baseline and the paper has no diversity or after-AI measure.
